title: Ops signal bridge for trace enrichment and runbook telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an ‘Ops Signal Bridge’ service that synthesizes traces/metrics/log snippets and injects structured context into PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident channels, while also surfacing runbook suggestions and seeding postmortem drafts. This ticket covers the integration points, payload schema, fallback policies, and the automation hooks for runbook insertion.

Progress summary:
- Jan 12: Kickoff and scope confirmed with PM and SRE. We decided to limit initial rollout to latency and 5xx error signals to keep noise low.
- Jan 18: Finalized enriched payload schema (trace_id, sampled_spans, top_error_frames, kv-cache-snippet, recent-console-logs, latency_histogram_slice, candidate_runbooks). Schema lives in Confluence (link below).
- Jan 22: Implemented trace sampler and lightweight evidence bundler (language: Go). Initial unit tests for trace snippet extraction added.
- Jan 28: PD connector prototype created — sends structured JSON attachment to PagerDuty events API v2 with ‘evidence_bundle’ field and a runbook_suggestions array. Service handles rate limiting and exponential backoff.
- Feb 02: Slack composer built to post an ops-summary thread with quick actions: Attach runbook, Open quickplaybook editor, Seal evidence bundle to incident. Buttons use our existing chatops framework.
- Feb 05: Integration test pipeline added; failing on one flaky test that hits long-tail trace fetch timeouts. We’re adding a cancellable fetch and a 500ms cache-backed fastpath for recent spans.

Decisions and trade-offs:
- We intentionally limit trace sampling to high-severity incidents to avoid ingest costs; sampling policy uses SLO breach + error-rate trigger.
- Chose to inline compressed KV snippets in attachments rather than host blobs behind signed URLs to keep the PD/Slack experience atomic; trade-off is size — we cap to 64KB and attach a hosted blob when over threshold.
- Runbook suggestions are generated by matching normalized span patterns against a curated set of runbooks and a small ML classifier (on-device heuristics). Initial version is whitelist-driven to reduce false positives.

Open risks / blockers:
- Long-tail trace retrieval causing timeouts (workaround: partial evidence + link to dashboard).
- Security review for attaching potentially sensitive logs (PR is in review with Security).
- Need SRE approval on PD suppression windows to avoid noisy duplicate incidents.

Next steps:
- Stabilize trace fetch path (assign to Marco, see tasks).
- Complete security review and add redaction pass for logs.
- Add canary on internal team PD integration for two weeks, collect false-positive metrics, and tune classifier thresholds.
- Wire postmortem draft seeding into autopopulate playbook flow (follow-on ticket if MVP is stable).

acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents receive a structured evidence_bundle attachment for sampled high-severity incidents
Slack incident threads include an ops-summary card with buttons: Attach runbook, Open editor, Seal evidence bundle

Evidence bundle size capped at 64KB with fallback hosted blob link
All attached logs are redacted for PII per Security review checklist
Integration tests pass in CI for PD and Slack connectors (flaky tolerance <1%)
